messages.content:
The writer's note about it, in their words: 我想在 r/WarriorCats 发一个提问帖，问问大家的看法。
A learner of English is rewriting part of a post for Reddit, question post:
<<<
I’m on the early chapters of Darktail’s Judgment, and I get a little bit confused about why StarClan didn’t show up when Darkpaw was at the moonstone and he got really miserable and furious about that.

Ravenpaw said StarClan had travelled with the Clans and left the forest skies, and it would be physically or magically hard to get back here for a distant little kittypet who wanted to join the Clans. But it was mentioned in the book that it was a overcast day, so without the moonlight it’s onlynatural that they couldn’t reach StarClan back then when the Clans were still in the forest. (Could someone tell me if there was a similar case in the other books that the night sky’s cloudy when a cat was at the Moonstone? Or does StarClan have the power to clear the clouds if they want to communicate?)

And Darkpaw didn’t go for another try on a clear day; he just chose to transform himself into Darktail👿 instead.
>>>
The part: "(Could someone tell me if there was a similar case in the other books that the night sky’s cloudy when a cat was at the Moonstone?"
What is wrong with it: English expects a direct question here, such as 'Has there been another time when...?' The 'if...where' chain under 'Could someone tell me' still makes the question hard to find at once.
What they mean (confirmed by them): Everything this passage says now: every point, question, hedge and feeling in it stays; only how it is put changes.
A version that works (never show it or any stretch of it): "(Does anyone know of a similar case in the other books where the night sky was cloudy when a cat was at the Moonstone?"
Words they already have as hints: anyone
Their last try: "(Could someone tell me if there was a similar case in the other books that the night sky’s cloudy when some cat’s at the Moonstone?"
What the tutor told them about it: Your version still opens with 'Could someone tell me if', so readers have to dig for the question. Also, 'the night sky’s cloudy when some cat’s at the Moonstone' is in the present tense, while your post is telling a past scene.
They are stuck. Write two hints that help them build it themselves, never giving them the wording:
- plan: in English, one or two short sentences, as their tutor: how a fluent writer builds this part: what comes first, what follows, how the parts connect (contrast, cause, addition) and where the emphasis goes. Start from their try: what to keep and what to build differently. Name no English word except the hint words above (none from the working version), no letter counts, no fill-in blanks. It is about the words of this part, never the content they talk about ("first the interactions between them, then…" plans a story, not the sentence). When the part is a word or two (left in Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China), or a missing word), say what kind of word goes there and how it sits in the sentence.
- example: one short English sentence a fluent writer would actually write (grammatical and natural on its own), about an everyday topic unrelated to the post (different people, things and events), built the same way as the working version: the same pattern and the same connecting words, none of its other content words. Put [square brackets] around the few words it shares with the working version as they are (the frame they can borrow, at most four), never around the words that change.
The writer may write to you in any language; whatever they write in, everything you write for them is in English.
Reply with JSON only: {"plan":"","example":""}

result.text: {"plan":"Keep every point you already make, but put the question itself at the very front and ask it straight, without a polite request or a hedge before it. Then make the verb forms match the scene you are describing, and link the cloudy night to the Moonstone with the same kind of connection you already use, so the whole thing reads as one clear question.","example":"[Does anyone know] a cafe in town [where] the coffee was hot when we walked in?"}
